5.13 Aqueous CuSO4 solution exists as [Cu(H2O)4]SO4 which has blue colour due to [Cu(H2O)4]2+ ions.
(i) When KF is added, the weak H2O ligands are replaced by F ̄ ligands, forming [CuF4]2" ions
which is a green precipitate.
[Cu(H2O)4]2+ + 4F– → [CuF4]2– + 4H2O
(ii) When KCl is added, Cl ̄ ligands replace the weak H2O ligands forming [CuCl4)2– ions which has
bright green colour.
[Cu(H2O)4]2+ + 4Cl– → [CuCl4]2– + 4H2O
5.14 [Cu(H2O)4]2+ + 4 CN– → [Cu(CN)4]2- + 4H2O
As CN ̄ is a strong ligand, it forms a highly stable complex with Cu2+ ion. On passing H2S, free Cu2+
ions are not available to form the precipitate of CuS.
